G0001G.def:
Α, α, ἄλφα (which see), τό, indecl., 
alpha, the first letter of the Greek alphabet. As a numeral, ά = 1, α = 1000. As a prefix, it appears to have at least two and perhaps three distinct senses: 
__1. ἀ- (before a vowel, ἀν-) negative, as in ἄ-γνωστος, ἄ-δικος. 
__2. ἀ-, ἁ- copulative, indicating community and fellowship, as in ἁ-πλοῦς, ἀ-κολουθέω, ἀ-δελφός. 
__3. An intensive force (LS, s. α), as in ἀ-τενίζω is sometimes assumed (but see Boisacq, see word).

G0002.def:
Ἀαρών (Heb. אַהֲרוֹן), indecl. (in FlJ, -ῶνος), 
Aaron (Exode 4:14, al.): Luc 1:5, Actes 7:40, Hébreux 5:4, 7:11, 9:4.†

G0003.def:
Ἀβαδδών (Heb. אֲבַדּוֹן, destruction; LXX, ἀπώλεια, only in Wisdom Lit., of the place of the ruined dead: Job 26:6, 28:22, 31:12, Psaumes 88:12, Proverbes 15:11*), indecl.; 
in NT, Abaddon, the angel of the Abyss: Apocalypse 9:11.†

G0004.def:
αβαρής, -ές 
(βαρός), 
without weight; metaphorically (MM, VGT, see word) not burdensome: 2 Corinthiens 11:9.†

G0005.def:
Ἀββά (T, -ᾶ), indecl. (Aram, אַבָּא, emphatic form of אַב = Heb. אָב, father), 
used in the phrase Ἀ. ὁ παήρ, Abba, Father (see Swete on Mk, I.with): Marc 14:36, Romains 8:15, Galates 4:6.†

G0006.def:
Ἄβελ, (WH, Ἅ-), ὁ, indecl. 
(הֶבֶל), 
Abel (Genèse 4:2-10): Hébreux 11:4, 12:24; αἵμα Ἄ., Matthieu 23:35, Luc 11:51.†

G0007G.def:
Ἀβιά (Heb. אֲבִיָּה, אֲבִיָּהוּ), ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἀβίας, -α), 
Abia, Abijah. 
__1. Son of Rehoboam (3Ki.14:1): Matthieu 1:7. 
__2. A priest of the line of Eleazar (1 Chroniques 24:3, 10): Luc 1:5. 
†

G0007H.def:
Ἀβιά (Heb. אֲבִיָּה, אֲבִיָּהוּ), ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἀβίας, -α), 
Abia, Abijah. 
__1. Son of Rehoboam (3Ki.14:1): Matthieu 1:7. 
__2. A priest of the line of Eleazar (1 Chroniques 24:3, 10): Luc 1:5. 
†

G0008.def:
Ἀβιάθαρ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. אֶבְיָתָר), 
Abiathar (1 Rois 21:1): Marc 2:26.†

G0009.def:
Ἀβειληνή (T, Rec. Ἀβι-), -ῆς, ἡ, (sc. χώρα), 
Abilene, a district in the Anti-Lebanon: Luc 3:1.†

G0010.def:
Ἀβιούδ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. אֲבִיָּהוּד), 
Abiud, Abihud: Matthieu 1:13.†

G0011.def:
Ἀβραάμ (Heb. אַבְרָהָם), ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἄβραμος, -ου; MM, VGT, see word), 
Abraham (Genèse 17:5 al.): Matthieu 1:1, 2 al.

G0014.def:
ἀγαθοεργέω, -ῶ, 
to do good, show kindness: 1 Ti 6:18 (Cremer, 8).†
ἀγαθουργέω, -ῶ, contracted form (rare, see WH, App., 145) of ἀγαθοερ- (which see), 
to do good: Actes 14:17.†

G0017.def:
ἀγαθοποιός, -όν = cl. ἀγαθουργός, 
[in LXX, of a woman who deals pleasantly in order to corrupt, Sir.42:14 * ;] 
doing well, acting rightly (Plut.): 1 Pierre 2:14 (Cremer, 8; MM, VGT, see word).†

G0018.def:
ἀγαθός, -ή, -όν, 
[in LXX chiefly for טוֹב ;] 
in general, good, in physical and in moral sense, used of persons, things, acts, conditions, etc., applied to that which is regarded as "perfect in its kind, so as to produce pleasure and satisfaction, . . . that which, in itself good, is also at once for the good and the advantage of him who comes in contact with it" (Cremer, 3): γῆ, Luc 8:8; δένδρον, Matthieu 7:18; καρδία, Luc 8:15; δόσις, Jacques 1:17; μέρις, Luc 10:42; ἔργον (frequently in Pl.), Philippiens 1:6; ἐλπίς, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:16; θησαυρός, Matthieu 12:35; μνεία, 1 Thessaloniciens 3:6 (cf. 2Ma.7:20); as subst., τὸ ἀ, that which is morally good, beneficial, acceptable to God, Romains 12:2; ἐργάζεσθαι τὸ ἀ, Romains 2:10, Éphésiens 4:28; πράσσειν, Romains 9:11, 2 Corinthiens 5:10; διώκειν, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:15; μιμεῖσθαι, III Jo 11; κολλᾶσθαι τῷ ἀ, Romains 12:9; ερωτᾶν περὶ τοῦ ἀ., Matthieu 19:17; διάκονος εἰς τὸ ἀ., Romains 13:4; τὸ ἀ. σου, thy favour, benefit, Phm 14; pl., τὰ ἀ., of goods, possessions, Luc 12:18; of spiritual benefits, Romains 10:15, Hébreux 9:11, 10:1. ἀ is opposite to πονηρός, Matthieu 5:45, 20:5; κακός, Romains 7:19; φαῦλος, Romains 9:11, 2 Corinthiens 5:10 (cf. MM, VGT, see word).
SYN.: καλός, δίκαιος. κ. properly refers to goodliness as manifested in form: ἀ. to inner excellence (cf. the cl. καλὸς κἀγαθός and ἐν καρδία κ. καὶ ἀ., Luc 8:15). In Romains 5:7, where it is contrasted with δ., ἀ. implies a kindliness and attractiveness not necessarily possessed by the δίκαιος, who merely measures up to a high standard of rectitude (cf. ἀγαθωσύνη).

G0019.def:
ἀγαθωσύνη (on the termination, see: ἁγιότης, and cf . WH, App., 152; MM, VGT, see word), -ης, ἡ 
(ἀγαθός), [in LXX for טוֹבָה, טוֹב, טוּב, only in Heb. bks. ;] 
goodness (representing "the kindlier, as δικαιοσύνη, the sterner element in the ideal character," AE, Eph., 5:9; on its relation to χρηστότης, see Tr., Syn., §lxiii): Romains 15:14, Galates 5:22, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:11.†

G0020.def:
ἀγαλλίασις, -εως, ἡ 
(ἀγαλλιάω), [in LXX (most frequently in Pss. and often coupled with εὐφροσύνη, as Ps 44(45):15) chiefly for גִּיל ;] 
exultation, exuberant joy: Luc 1:44, Actes 2:46, Hébreux 1:9, Ju 24; χαρὰ καὶ ἀ., Luc 1:14 (Cremer, 592).†

G0022.def:
ἄ-γαμος, -ον 
[in LXX: 4Ma.16:9 * ;] 
unmarried: 1 Corinthiens 7:8, 32; fem. (= cl. ἄνανδρος), ib. 11, 34.†

G0023.def:
ἀγανακτέω, -ῶ (ἄγαν, much, ἄχομαι, to grieve), 
[in LXX: Wis.5:22, 12:27, Da TH Bel 28, 4Ma.4:21 * ;] 
to be indignant: Matthieu 21:15, 26:8, Marc 10:14, 14:4; before περί, Matthieu 20:24, Marc 10:41; before ὅτι, Luc 13:14 (see MM, VGT, see word).†

G0024.def:
ἀγανάκτησις, -εως, ἡ 
(ἀγανακτέω), [in LXX: Esther 18:3 א 1 * ;] 
indignation: 2 Corinthiens 7:11 (see MM, VGT, see word).†

G0025.def:
ἀγαπάω, -ῶ, 
[in LXX chiefly for אהב ;] 
to love, to feel and exhibit esteem and goodwill to a person, to prize and delight in a thing. 
__1. Of human affection, to men: τ. πλησίον, Matthieu 5:43; τ. ἐχθρούς, ib. 44; to Christ, Jean 8:42; to God, Matthieu 22:37; with accusative of thing(s), Luc 11:43, Jean 12:43, Éphésiens 5:25, II Tim 4:8, 10, Hébreux 1:9, 1 Pierre 2:17, 3:10, 2 Pierre 2:15, 1 Jean 2:15, Apocalypse 12:11.
__2. Of divine love; 
__(a) God's love: to men, Romains 8:37; to Christ, Jean 3:35; 
__(b) Christ's love: to men, Marc 10:21; to God, Jean 14:31; with cogn. accusative, Jean 17:26, Éphésiens 2:4.
SYN.: φιλέω. From its supposed etymology (Thayer, LS; but see also Boisacq) ἀ. is commonly understood properly to denote love based on esteem (diligo), as distinct from that expressed by φιλέω (amo), spontaneous natural affection, emotional and unreasoning. If this distinction holds, ἀ. is fitly used in NT of Christian love to God and man, the spiritual affection which follows the direction of the will, and which, therefore, unlike that feeling which is instinctive and unreasoned, can be commanded as a duty. (Cf. ἀγάπη, and v. Tr., Syn. §xii; Cremer, 9, 592; and esp. MM, VGT, see word)

G0026.def:
ἀγάπη, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX for אַהֲבָה, which is also rendered by ἀγάπησις and φιλία ;] 
love, goodwill, esteem. Outside of bibl. and eccl. books, there is no clear instance (with Deiss., LAE, 18:4, 70:2, cf. the same writer in Constr. Quar., ii, 4; and with MM, VGT, see word, cf. Dr. Moulton in Exp. Times, xxvi, 3, 139). In NT, like ἀγαπάω, -ῶ, 
__1. Of men's love: 
__(a) to one another, Jean 13:35; 
__(b) to God, 1 Jean 2:5.
__2. Of divine love; 
__(a) God's love: to men, Romains 5:8; to Christ, Jean 17:26; 
__(b) Christ's love to men: Romains 8:35. 
__3. In pl., love feasts: Ju 12 (DB, iii, 157).
SYN.: φιλία. ἀ., signifying properly (see: ἀγαπάω) love which chooses its object, is taken over from LXX, where its connotation is more general, into NT, and there used exclusively to express that spiritual bond of love between God and man and between man and man, in Christ, which is characteristic of Christianity. It is thusdistinct from φιλία, friendship (Jacques 4:4 only), στοργή, natural affection (in NT only in compounds, see: ἄστοργος) and ἔρως, sexual love, which is not used in NT, its place being taken by ἐπιθυμία. (Cf. ἀγαπάω; and see Abbott, Essays, 70f.; DB, vol. i., 555; Cremer, 13, 593; MM, VGT, see word).

G0028.def:
Ἅγαρ (Rec. Ἄ-), ἡ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἀγάρα, -ης, Heb. הָגָר), 
Hagar (Gen.16): Galates 4:24,25.†

G0029.def:
ἀγγαρεύω (from the Persian; cf. Vg. angiare, and the Heb. אִגֶרֶת; on the orthogr., see Bl., §6, 1; M, Pr., 46), 
to impress into public service, employ a courier; hence, to compel to perform a service (prob. common in the vernac.; cf. Deiss., BS, 86f., MM, Exp., iv; VGT, see word): Matthieu 5:41, 27:32, Marc 15:21.†

G0030.def:
ἀγγεῖον, -ου, τό 
(ἄγγος), [in LXX chiefly for כְּלִי ;] 
a vessel (see MM, VGT, see word): Matthieu 25:4.†

G0031.def:
ἀγγελία, -ας, ἡ 
(ἄγγελος), [in LXX chiefly for שְׁמוּעָה ;] 
a message: 1Jo.1:5, 3:11 (Cremer, 18; MM, VGT, see word).†

G0032G.def:
ἄγγελος, -ου, ὁ, 
[in LXX chiefly for מַלְאָךְ ;] 
__1. a messenger, one sent: Matthieu 11:10, Jacques 22:25.
__2. As in LXX, in the special sense of angel, a spiritual, heavenly being, attendant upon God and employed as his messenger to men, to make known his purposes, as Luc 1:11, or to execute them, as Matthieu 4:6. The ἄ. in Apocalypse 1:20-2:1, al., is variously understood as 
__(1) a messenger or delegate, 
__(2) a bishop or ruler, 
__(3) a guardian angel, 
__(4) the prevailing spirit of each church, i.e. the Church itself. (Cf. Swete, Ap)., in l.; DB, iv, 991; Thayer, see word; Cremer, 18; MM, VGT, see word)

G0032H.def:
ἄγγελος, -ου, ὁ, 
[in LXX chiefly for מַלְאָךְ ;] 
__1. a messenger, one sent: Matthieu 11:10, Jacques 22:25.
__2. As in LXX, in the special sense of angel, a spiritual, heavenly being, attendant upon God and employed as his messenger to men, to make known his purposes, as Luc 1:11, or to execute them, as Matthieu 4:6. The ἄ. in Apocalypse 1:20-2:1, al., is variously understood as 
__(1) a messenger or delegate, 
__(2) a bishop or ruler, 
__(3) a guardian angel, 
__(4) the prevailing spirit of each church, i.e. the Church itself. (Cf. Swete, Ap)., in l.; DB, iv, 991; Thayer, see word; Cremer, 18; MM, VGT, see word)

G0034.def:
ἀγέλη, -ης, ἡ 
(ἄγω), [in LXX chiefly for עֵ֫דֶר ;] 
a herd: Matthieu 8:30-32, Marc 5:11, 13, Luc 8:32,33.†

G0035.def:
ἀγενεαλόγητος, -ον 
(γενεαλογέω), 
without genealogy, i.e. without recorded pedigree (cf. Néhémie 7:64): Hébreux 7:3 (Cremer, 152; MM, VGT, see word).†

G0036.def:
ἀγενής, -ές 
(γένος), 
__1. unborn (Plat.); 
__2. of no family, ignoble, base (opposite to ἀγαθός, Soph., Fr., 105): opposite to εὐγενής, 1 Corinthiens 1:28 (for exx. from π., see MM, VGT, see word). 
†

G0037.def:
ἁγιάζω, Hellenistic form of ἁγίζω 
(ἅγιος), 
to make holy, consecrate, sanctify; [in LXX chiefly for קדשׁ pi., hi. ;] 
__1. to dedicate, separate, set apart for God; of things: Matthieu 23:17,19, 2 Timothée 2:21; of persons: Christ, Jean 10:36, 17:19.
__2. to purify, make conformable in character to such dedication: forensically, to free from guilt, 1 Corinthiens 6:11, Éphésiens 5:26, Hébreux 2:11, 10:10, 14, 29, 13:12; internally, by actual sanctification of life, Jean 17:17, 19, Actes 20:32, 26:18, Romains 15:16, 1 Corinthiens 1:2, 7:14, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:23, Apocalypse 22:11; of a nonbeliever influenced by marriage with a Christian, 1 Corinthiens 7:14.
__3. In the intermediate sense of ceremonial or levitical purification: 
__(a) of things, 2 Timothée 2:21; 
__(b) of persons, Hébreux 9:13. 
__4. to treat as holy: Matthieu 6:9, Luc 11:2, 1 Pierre 3:16 (Cremer, 53, 602; MM, VGT, see word).
†

G0038.def:
ἁγιασμός, -οῦ, ὁ 
(ἁγιάζω), [in LXX: Eze.45:4 (מִקְדָּשׁ), Sir.7:31, etc. ;] 
as an active verbal noun in -μός, it signifies properly the process τὸ ἁγιάζειν, rather than the resultant state, ἁγιωσύνη, hence, 
__1. consecration; 
__2. sanctification: so strictly in Romains 6:19,22 (but see Meyer), 1 Corinthiens 1:30, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:3,7, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:13, Hébreux 12:14, 1 Pierre 1:2. Elsewhere it perhaps (Ellic.; but see Milligan, Th., 48) inclines to the resultant state: 1 Thessaloniciens 4:4, 1 Timothée 2:15 (Cremer, 55, 602).
†

G0039G.def:
ἅγιος, -α, ον 
(τό ἅγός, religious awe; ἅζω, to venerate), [in LXX chiefly for קֹ֫דֶשׁ ;] 
primarily, dedicated to the gods, sacred (Hdt.; rare in Att., never in Hom., Hes. and Trag., who use ἁγνός), hence, holy, characteristic of God, separated to God, worthy of veneration. 
__1. Its highest application is to God himself, in his purity, majesty, and glory: Luc 1:49, Jean 17:11, Apocalypse 4:8. Hence 
__(a) of things and places which have a claim to reverence as sacred to God, e.g. the Temple: Matthieu 24:15, Hébreux 9:1; 
__(b) of persons employed by him, as angels: 1 Thessaloniciens 3:13; prophets, Luc 1:70; apostles, Éphésiens 3:5. 
__2. Applied to persons as separated to God's service: 
__(a) of Christ, Marc 1:24, Jean 6:69, Actes 4:30; 
__(b) of Christians, Actes 9:13, Romains 1:7, Hébreux 6:10, Apocalypse 5:8. 
__3. In the moral sense of sharing God's purity: Marc 6:20, Jean 17:11, Actes 3:14, Apocalypse 3:7.
__4. Of pure, clean sacrifices and offerings: 1 Corinthiens 7:14, Éphésiens 1:4. 
SYN.: ἁγνός, pure, both in ceremonial and spiritual sense; ἱερός (sacer), sacred, that which is inviolable because of its (external) relation to God; ὅσιος (sanctus as opposite to nefas), that which is based on everlasting ordinances of right. (Cf. Tr., Syn., §lxxxviii; DB, ii, 399 f.; Cremer, 34, 594-601; MM, VGT, see word)

G0041.def:
ἁγιότης, -ητος, ἡ 
(ἅγιος), [in LXX: 2Ma.15:2 * ;] 
sanctity, holiness, regarded, properly, as an abstract quality (see next word, and cf. Lft. Notes, 49; MM, VGT, see word): 2 Corinthiens 1:12, Hébreux 12:10.†

G0042.def:
ἁγιωσύνη (cf. ἀγαθωσύνη), -ης, ἡ 
(ἅγιος), [in LXX: Psa.29 (30):4 96(97):12 (קֹדֶשׁ), 95(96):6 (עֹז), 144(145):5 (הוֹד), 2Ma.3:12 * ;] 
holiness, the state in man resulting from ἁγιασμός, which see: Romains 1:4, 2 Corinthiens 7:1, 1 Thessaloniciens 3:13 (Cremer, 52; MM, VGT, see word).†

G0043.def:
ἀγκάλη,-ης, ἡ 
(ἄγκος, a bend), [in LXX for אַצִּיל, חֵיק ;] 
the bent arm: Luc 2:28 (cf. ἐναγκαλίζομαι).†

G0044.def:
ἄγκιστρον, -ου, τό 
(ἄγκος, a bend), [in LXX חַכָּה, etc. ;] 
a fish-hook: Matthieu 17:27.†

G0045.def:
ἄγκυρα, -ας, ἡ (ἄγκος, a bend), [in Sm.: Jérémie 52:18 * ;]
an anchor: Actes 27:29, 30 40 ; figuratively (MM, VGT, see word), Hébreux 6:19.†

G0046.def:
ἄγναφος, -ον (= ἄγναπτος, γνάπτω, late form of κνάπτω, to card wool), 
uncarded, undressed, i.e. new (MM, VGT, see word): Matthieu 92:6, Marc 2:21.†

G0047.def:
ἁγνεία (WH, ἁγνία), 
[in LXX for טָהֳרָה, נָזִיר, נֶזֶר, etc. ;] 
purity: 1 Timothée 4:12, 5:2 (Cremer, 58. For exx. of ceremonial use in π., see MM, Exp., iv).†

G0049.def:
ἁγνισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (> ἁγνίζω), 
[in LXX: Nombres 6:5 (נֵזֶר) 8:7 19:17 (חַטָּאָה), etc. ;] 
purification: in ceremonial sense, Actes 21:26 (LXX).†

G0050.def:
ἀγνοέω, -ῶ (> ἁγνίζω), 
[in LXX for שָׁגָה, שָׁגַג, אָשַׁם, etc. ;] 
__1. to be ignorant, not to know: absol., Ι Ti 1:13, Hébreux 5:2; with accusative, Actes 13:27 17:23, Romains 10:3, 2 Corinthiens 2:11; ἐν οἷς, 2 Pierre 2:12; before ὅτι, Romains 2:4 6:3 7:1, 1 Corinthiens 14:38; οὐ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, a Pauline phrase: with accusative, Romains 11:25; before ὑπέρ, 2 Corinthiens 1:8; περί, 1 Corinthiens 12:1, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:13. ὅτι, Romains 1:13, 1 Corinthiens 10:1 (for similar usage in π., V. MM, VGT, see word). Pass.: 1 Corinthiens 14:38, 2 Corinthiens 6:9, Galates 1:22.
__2. not to understand: with accusative, Marc 9:32, Luc 9:45.
†

G0051.def:
ἀγνόημα, -τός, τό 
(ἀγνοέω), [in LXX: Genèse 43:12 (מִשְׁגֶּה), Tob.3:3, Jdth.5:20, Sir.23:2 51:19, 1Ma.13:39 * ;] 
a sin of ignorance (so in π.; see MM, VGT, see word): Hébreux 9:7.†

G0052.def:
ἄγνοια, -ας, ἡ 
(ἀγνοέω), [in LXX chiefly for אָשָׁם, שְׁגָגָה ;] 
ignorance : Actes 3:17 17:30, Éphésiens 4:18 (with sense of wilful blindness; cf. MM, VGT, see word), 1 Pierre 1:14.†

G0053.def:
ἁγνός, -ή, -όν 
(ἅγος, see: ἅγιος), [in LXX chiefly for טָהוֹר (Pss, and Pr. only), also 2Ma.13:8, 4Ma.18:7, al. ;] 
__1. free from ceremonial defilement, in a condition prepared for worship (for exx. of pagan usage, V. MM, VGT, see word). 
__2. holy, sacred, venerable (II Mac, l.with). 
__3. As in OT (cl.), pure, chaste, undefiled, guiltless; 
__(a) of persons: 2 Corinthiens 7:11 11:12, 1 Timothée 5:22, Tite 2:5, 1 Jean 3:3; 
__(b) of things: Philippiens 4:8, Jacques 3:17, 1 Pierre 3:2.
† SYN.: εἰλικρινής (which see), pure, primarily as winnowed, purged, first found in ethical sense in NT (sincere). On the equivalence of ἁ. and καθαρός (which see), see DCG, ii, 459a though Westc. (Epp. Jo., 101) notes a distinction between them.

G0054.def:
ἁγνότης, -τητος, ἡ 
(ἁγνός), 
purity, chastity (cf. ἁγιότης): 2 Corinthiens 6:6 11:3.†

G0056.def:
ἀγνωσία, -ας, ἡ 
(γινώσκω), [in LXX: Job 35:16 (בִּבְלִי־דַּעַת), Wis.13:1, 3Ma.5:27 * ;] 
ignorance (opposite to γνῶσις): 1 Corinthiens 15:34, 1 Pierre 2:15 (see Hort in l.; MM, VGT, see word).†

G0057.def:
ἄγνωστος, -ον 
(γινώσκω), [in LXX: Wis.11:18 18:3, 2Ma.1:19 2:7 (Cremer, 157) * ;] 
unknown: Actes 17:23 (cf. MM, VGT, see word).†

G0058.def:
ἀγορά, -ας, ἡ (ἀγείρω, to bring together) 
[in LXX for עִזָּבוֹן, שׁוּק ;] 
__1. an assembly (Hom., Xen., al.).
__2. a place of assembly, a public place or forum, a market-place (Hom., Thuc, al.; LXX): Matthieu 11:16 20:2 23:7, Marc 6:56 (cf . MM, VGT, see word, ἀγυιά) 7:4 (Bl., §46, 7) 12:38, Luc 7:32 (Bl., l.with) 11:43 20:46, Actes 16:19 17:7 (Cremer, 59; MM, VGT, see word).
†

G0059.def:
ἀγοράζω 
(ἀγορά), [in LXX chiefly for שׁבר, קנה ;] 
__1. to frequent the ἀγορά (Hdt., al.). 
__2. to buy in the market, purchase (Xen., al.; LXX; in π. very common in deeds of sale, see MM, VGT, see word): absol., Matthieu 21:12, Marc 11:15; with accusative of thing(s), Matthieu 13:44, 46, al.; before παρά, with genitive of person(s), Apocalypse 3:18 (LXX, Polyb.); ἐκ, Matthieu 27:7; with genitive pret., Marc 6:37, al.; metaphorically, 1 Corinthiens 6:20 7:23, 2 Pierre 2:1, Apocalypse 5:9 14:3, 4.

G0060.def:
ἀγοραῖος, -ον 
(ἀγορά), 
__1. frequenting the ἀγορά , a lounger in the ἀγορά (Xen., al.): Actes 17:5. 
__2. In late writers (Strab., al.), proper to the ἀγορά : ἀγοραῖοι (sc. ἥμεραι) ἀγονται (cf. Lat. conventus agere), court-days are kept, Actes 19:38 (for exx. of both usages, see MM, VGT, see word).
†

G0061.def:
ἄγρα, -ας, ἡ 
(ἄγω), 
__1. the chase, a hunting or catching: Luc 5:4. 
__2. that which is taken, a catch: of fish, Luc 5:9. 
†

G0062.def:
ἀγραυλέω, -ῶ 
(ἀγραυλος, dwelling in the field; ἀγρός, αὐλή), 
to live in the fields: Luc 2:8.†

G0063.def: to dwell in the field , (New Testament) (ML)

G0064.def:
ἀγρεύω (ἄγρα), 
[in LXX: Job 10:16, Proverbes 5:22 6:25,26, Osée 5:2 (לקח ni., שׁחט, etc.)* ;] 
to catch or take by hunting or fishing; metaphorically, Marc 12:13.†

G0065.def:
ἀγρι-έλαιος, -ον
__1. of the wild olive (Anth.). 
__2. As subst., the wild olive: Romains 11:17, 24 (CGT, in 1.; MM, VGT, see word).
†

G0066.def:
ἄγριος, -α, -ον 
(ἀγρός), [in LXX for שָׂדֶה, etc. ;] 
__1. living in fields, wild: μέλι. Matthieu 3:4, Marc 1:6. 
__2. savage, fierce: Ju 13. (Cf. usage in π. of a malignant wound; MM, VGT, see word)
†

G0067.def:
Ἀγρίππας, -α (Bl., §7, 2), ὁ
Agrippa (II): Actes 25:13, 22, 23, 24, 26 26:1, 2, 19, 27, 28, 32. (For Agrippa I, see: Ἡρῴδης, 3.) †

G0068G.def:
ἀγρός, -οῦ, ὁ, 
[in LXX chiefly for שָׂדֶה ]; 
__1. a field: Matthieu 6:28, al. 
__2. the country: Marc 15:21, al.; pl., country places, farms: Marc 5:14 6:36 56, Luc 8:34 9:12. 
__3. = χωρίον a piece of ground: Marc 10:29, Actes 4:27, al. (On the occurrence of this word as compared with χώρα, χωρίον see MM, VGT, see word)

G0068H.def:
ἀγρός, -οῦ, ὁ, 
[in LXX chiefly for שָׂדֶה ]; 
__1. a field: Matthieu 6:28, al. 
__2. the country: Marc 15:21, al.; pl., country places, farms: Marc 5:14 6:36 56, Luc 8:34 9:12. 
__3. = χωρίον a piece of ground: Marc 10:29, Actes 4:27, al. (On the occurrence of this word as compared with χώρα, χωρίον see MM, VGT, see word)

G0069.def:
ἀγρυπνέω, -ῶ (ἄγρυπνος, seeking sleep ; ἀγρεύω, ὕπνος), 
[in LXX chiefly for שׁקד ;] 
to be sleepless, wakeful (Theogn., Xen., al.); metaphorically (LXX) = cl. ἐγρήγορα, to be watchful, vigilant: Marc 13:33, Luc 21:36, Éphésiens 6:18, Hébreux 13:17.†
SYN.: γρηγορέω, which see; νήφω, associated with γ. in 1 Pierre 5:8, expressing a wariness which results from self-control, a condition of moral, not merely mental alertness (see M, Th., I, 5:6).

G0070.def:
ἀγρυπνία, -ας, ἡ (see supr.), 
[in LXX: Si .9, 2Ma.2:26 * ;] 
sleeplessness, watching: 2 Corinthiens 6:5 11:27. (Plat., Hdt.; for exx. in π., see MM, VGT, see word) †

G0071.def:
ἄγω, 
[in LXX for בּוא hi., לקח, נהג, etc. ;] 
__1. to lead, bring, carry: with ace, before ἐπί, εἰς, ἕως, πρός and simple dative; metaphorically, to lead, guide, impel: Jean 10:16 Romains 2:4, Hébreux 2:10, 2 Timothée 3:6, al. 
__2. to spend or keep a day: Luc 24:21, Actes 19:38 
__3. Intrans., to go: subjunc., ἄγωμεν, Matthieu 2:46, al. (Cramer, 61; MM, VGT, see word).

G0072.def:
ἀγωγή, -ῆς, ἡ 
(ἄγω), [in LXX: Esther 2:20 10:3, 2Ma.4:16 6:8 11:24, 3Ma.4:10 * ;] 
__1. a carrying away. 
__2. a leading, guiding; metaphorically, training; hence, from the expression ἀ. τοῦ βίου, absol., conduct, way of life: 2 Timothée 3:10 (Cremer, 61; MM, VGT, see word).
†

G0073.def:
ἀγών, -ῶνος, ὁ 
(ἄγω), [in LXX: Ésaïe 7:13 (לאה), Esther 4:17, Wis.4:2 10:12, II Mac.6, 4Mac .5 * ;] 
__1. a gathering, esp. for games. 
__2. a place of assembly. 
__3. a contest, struggle, trial; metaphorically (MM, VGT, see word), 
__(a) of the Christian life as a contest and struggle: Philippiens 1:30, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:2, 1 Timothée 6:12, 2 Timothée 4:7 Hébreux 12:1;
__(b) solicitude, anxiety: Colossiens 2:1.
†

G0074.def:
ἀγωνία, -ας, ἡ 
(ἀγών), [in LXX: 2Ma.3:14,16 15:19 * ;] 
__1. a contest, wrestling (Eur., Xen.). 
__2. Of the mind, great fear, agony, anguish (Dem., Arist.): Luc 22:44 (cf . Field, Notes, 77 f. ; Abbott, Essays, 101 f. ; MM, VGT, see word).
†

G0075.def:
ἀγωνίζομαι 
(ἀγών), [in LXX: Da TH 6:14 (שׂוּם בָּל), Sir.4:28, I, II, 4Mac .5 * ;] 
__1. to contend for a prize: 1 Corinthiens 9:25, 
__2. to fight, struggle, strive: Jean 18:36; metaphorically (MM, VGT, see word). Colossiens 1:29 4:12, 1 Timothée 4:10 6:12, 2 Timothée 4:7; with inf. (Field, Notes, 66), Luc 13:24 (Cremer, 609)
†

G0076.def:
Ἀδάμ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. אָדָם), 
Adam: Luc 3:38, Romains 5:14, 1 Corinthiens 15:22,45, 1 Timothée 2:13,14 Ju 14. Christ ὁ ἔσχατος Ἀ., 1 Corinthiens 15:45.†

G0077.def:
ἀδάπανος, -ον 
(δαπάνη), 
without expense, free of charge: 1 Corinthiens 9:18.†

G0079.def:
ἀδελφή, -ῆς, ἡ 
(ἀδελφός), [in LXX for אָהוֹת ;] 
a sister: Matthieu 19:29, al.; metaphorically (MM, VGT, see word), of a member of the Christian community: Romains 16:1, 1 Corinthiens 7:15 Jacques 21:15, al.

G0080.def:
ἀδελφός, -οῦ, ὁ 
(ἀ- copul., δελφύς, womb), 
in cl., a brother, born of the same parent or parents. [In LXX (Hort, Ja., 102f.), for אָח ;] 
__1. lit. of a brother (Genèse 4:2, al.). 
__2. Of a neighbour (Lévitique 19:17). 
__3. Of a member of the same nation (Exode 2:14, Deutéronome 15:3). In NT in each of these senses (1. Matthieu 1:2, al.; 2. Matthieu 7:3; 3. Romains 9:3) and also, 
__4. of a fellow-Christian: 1 Corinthiens 1:1, Actes 9:30. This usage finds illustration in π., where ἀ. is used of members of a pagan religious community (M, Th., I, 1:4; MM, VGT, see word). The ἀδελφοὶ τ. Κυρίου (Matthieu 12:46-49 13:55 28:10, Marc 3:31-34, Luc 8:19-21, Jean 2:12 7:3, 5 10 20:17, Actes 1:14, 1 Corinthiens 9:5) may have been sons of Joseph and Mary (Mayor, Ja., Intr. viff.; DB, i, 320ff.) or of Joseph by a former marriage (Lft., Gal., 252ff.; DCG, i, 232ff.), but the view of Jerome, which makes ἀ. equivalent to ἀνεψιός, is inconsistent with Greek usage. (Cremer, 66.)

G0081.def:
ἀδελφότης, -ητος, ἡ 
(ἀδελφός), [in LXX: 1Ma.12:10,17, 4Mac .5 * ;] 
__1. abstract, brotherhood, brotherly affection (LXX). 
__2. Concrete, the brotherhood, the Christian community: 1 Pierre 2:17 5:9 (MM, VGT, see word).
†

G0082.def:
ἄ-δηλος, -ον 
(δῆλος), [in LXX: Ps 50 (51):6 (בַּטֻחוֹת) ;] 
__1. unseen, unobserved, not manifest (Ps, l.with): Luc 11:44. 
__2. uncertain, indistinct: 1 Corinthiens 14:8.
†

G0084.def:
ἀδήλως 
(ἄδηλος), 
adv. uncertainly: of direction, 1 Corinthiens 9:26.†

G0085.def:
ἀδημονέω, -ῶ (on the derivation, see MM, VGT, see word), [in Aq.: Job 18:20; Sm.: Psa.60 (61):3 115:2 (116:11), Ecclésiaste 7:17(16), Eze.3:15 * ;] 
to be troubled, distressed (MM, l.with): Matthieu 26:37, Marc 14:33, Philippiens 2:26.†

G0086.def:
ᾅδης, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX ehiefly for שְׁאוֹל, also for דּוּמָה, מָוֶת, etc. ;] 
__1. in Hom., Hades (Pluto), the god of the underworld. 
__2. the abode of Hades, the underivorld; in NT, the abode of departed spirits, Hades: ἐν τ. ᾅ., Luc 16:23; εἰς ᾅ., Actes 2:27,31; πύλαι ᾅδου, Matthieu 16:18; κλεῖς τοῦ ᾅ., Apocalypse 1:18; metaphorically, ἕως ᾅ., Matthieu 11:23, Luc 10:15; personified, Apocalypse 6:8 20:13,14 (Cremer, 67, 610; MM, VGT, see word).
†

G0087.def:
ἀ-διά-κριτος, -ον 
(διακρίνω), [in LXX: Proverbes 25:1 * ;] 
__1. not to be parted, mixed, undistinguishable (cf. Pr, l.with, and see Lft., Ignat. Eph., §3). 
__2. without uncertainty (Hort, in l., but see MM, VGT, see word): Jacques 3:17.
†

G0088.def:
ἀδιάλειπτος, -ον 
(διαλείπω), 
unremitting, incessant: Romains 9:2, 2 Timothée 1:3. (For exx., see MM, VGT, see word) †

G0089.def:
ἀδιαλείπτως (see supr.), adv., 
[in LXX: 1Ma.12:11, II Mac .4, 3Ma.6:33 * ;] 
unremittingly, incessantly: Romains 1:9, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:3 2:13 5:17.†

G0091.def:
ἀδικέω, -ῶ 
(ἄδικος), [in LXX for עשׁק, עוה, etc. ;] 
__1. intrans., to be ἄδικος, do wrong, act wickedly or criminally: Actes 25:11, 1 Corinthiens 6:8, 2 Corinthiens 7:12, Colossiens 3:25, Apocalypse 22:11; to do hurt, Apocalypse 9:19. 
__2. Trans. 
__(a) to do some wrong: ὃ ἠδίκησεν, Colossiens 3:25; to wrong some one, Matthieu 20:13, Actes 7:26, 27 25:10, 2 Corinthiens 7:2, Galates 4:12, Phm 18, 2 Pierre 2:13; pass., Actes 7:24, 2 Corinthiens 7:12; mid., 1 Corinthiens 6:7 (suffer . . . to be wronged; WM, §38, 3; but see Bl., §54, 5; and cf. ἀποστερέω); 
__(b) to injure, hurt: Luc 10:19 Apocalypse 2:11 6:6 7:2, 3 9:4,10 11:5. 
†

G0092.def:
ἀδίκημα, -τος, τό 
(ἀδικέω), [in LXX for עָוֹן, פֶּשַׁע, etc. ;] 
a wrong, injury, misdeed (MM, VGT, see word): Actes 18:14 24:20, Apocalypse 18:5.†

G0093.def:
ἀδικία, -ας, ἡ 
(ἄδικος), [in LXX for עָוֹן, פֶּשַׁע, עָוֶל, etc. ;] 
__1. injustice: Luc 18:6, Romains 9:14. 
__2. unrighteousness, iniquity: Jean 7:18, Actes 8:23, Romains 1:18, 29 2:8 6:13, 2 Timothée 2:19, 1 Jean 1:9 5:17; opposite to ἀλήθεια, 1 Corinthiens 13:6, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:12; to δικαιοσύνη ], Romains 3:5; ἀπάτη τῆς ἀ., 2 Thessaloniciens 2:10; μισθὸς ἀδικίας, Actes 1:18, 2 Pierre 2:13,15; ἐγράται τῆς ἀ., Luc 13:27; μαμωνᾶς τῆς ἀ., Luc 16:9; κόσμος τῆς ἀ., Jacques 3:6; οἰκονόμος τῆς ἀ., Luc 16:8. 
__3. = ἀδίκημα, an unrighteous act: ironically, a favour, 2 Corinthiens 12:13; pl., Hébreux 8:12 (Cremer, 261; MM, VGT, see word).
†

G0094.def:
ἄδικος, -ον 
(δίκη), [in LXX for שׁקר, עול, etc. ;] 
__1. unjust: Romains 3:5, Hébreux 6:10. 
__2. unrighteous, wicked: Luc 16:11 18:11, Actes 24:15, 1 Corinthiens 6:1,9 1 Pierre 3:18; opposite to δίκαιος, Matthieu 5:45; to εὐσεβής, 2 Pierre 2:9; to πιστός, Luc 16:10 (Cremer, 200).
†

G0095.def:
ἀδίκως, adv. 
(ἄδικος), [in LXX for שׁקר, עול, etc. ;] 
unjustly, undeservedly: 1 Pierre 2:19.†

G0096.def:
ἀ-δόκιμος, -ον, 
[in LXX: Proverbes 25:4, Ésaïe 1:22 (סִיג) * ;] 
__1. of things (prop. of metals: LXX, ll. with), not standing the test, rejected: γῆ, Hébreux 6:8. 
__2. Of persons, rejected after testing, reprobate: Romains 1:28, 1 Corinthiens 9:27, 2 Corinthiens 13:5-7, 2 Timothée 3:8, Tite 1:16 (Cremer, 212).
†

G0097.def:
ἄδολος, -ον, 
__1. guileless (Pind., Thuc). 
__2. Of liquids (Æsch., Eur., and late prose writers), genuine, pure (in π. and in MGr. of wine, also of corn: MM, VGT, see word; Milligan, NTD, 77): of milk, metaphorically, 1 Pierre 2:2. 
† SYN.: ἀκέραιος (which see), ἄκακος, ἁπλοῦς.

G0098.def:
Ἁδραμυντηνός (T, Rec. Ἀδραμυττηνός), -ή,-όν, 
of Adramyttium, a seaport of Mysia: Actes 27:2.†

G0099.def:
Ἁδρίας (T, Rec. Ἀδρίας), -ου, ὁ, 
the Adriatic sea, in later Greek usage extended to take in all the waters between Greece and Italy: Actes 27:27.†
